claims.claim_vi: The source quotes Rob Pike (written "Rob Pyke"), one of the creators of Go: concurrency is about dealing with lots of things at once, parallelism about doing lots of things at once; concurrency is about design and parallelism about execution.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Concurrency structures a program to handle multiple tasks that can start, run and complete in overlapping periods but not necessarily at the same instant; it is the composition of independently executing processes and lets a program make progress on tasks without finishing one before starting another.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Parallelism is the simultaneous execution of multiple computations using multiple processors or cores; it requires hardware with multiple processing units and aims at throughput and computational speed.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Concurrency keeps a program responsive, runs background tasks and handles many operations even on a single core; useful for I/O-bound and high-latency work. Parallelism matters for CPU-bound tasks: heavy mathematics, data analysis, image processing, real-time processing.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Effective Go: concurrency is structuring a program as independently executing components, parallelism is executing calculations in parallel for efficiency on multiple CPUs; Go is a concurrent language, not a parallel one, though its concurrency features can make some problems easy to structure as parallel computations.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Python asyncio is a library to write concurrent code with async/await and is often a perfect fit for IO-bound and high-level structured network code.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Python threading: in CPython, due to the GIL, only one thread can execute Python code at once; to make better use of multi-core machines use multiprocessing or ProcessPoolExecutor; threading remains appropriate for running multiple I/O-bound tasks simultaneously.
